newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close with trimmed gains.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close with trimmed gains.

text.p: Late selling by speculators trimmed early gains as Delhi shares closed higher but off their peaks on the first day of the settlement period on Monday, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's Sensitive Index ended 5.12 points higher at 865.49 points. The index had surged to 872.72 in early trade.
Traders said investors were waiting for a government decision on petroleum prices before creating fresh positions.

"Despite rising trends, the fate of the market would depend on the meeting of the United Front later this week to consider the petroleum price hike issue," said Harjit Wadhwa of brokers Wadhwa Associates.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Saturday that the United Front will decide whether to raise the prices of domestic petroleum products at the coalition's next meeting, set for June 27.

At its last meeting on June 16, the 15-party United Front postponed a decision on whether to raise prices to plug the government's mounting debt to state oil companies, estimated at 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) at the end of March.
Leftwing parties in Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's alliance have strongly opposed any price increase.

Reliance Industries remained in fancy, ending 7.40 rupees higher at 367.40 on sustained buying by financial institutions and speculators in anticipation that the company will announce a bonus share issue later this week, brokers said.
The company's board of directors is scheduled to meet on June 26 to discuss a bonus share issue.

ITC slipped 3.45 rupees to 499.10 on profit-taking. The company announced it had signed an agreement with Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc on licensing of the BAT brand to ITC. The Calcutta-based company provided no details.
State Bank of India surged 16.70 rupees to 340.65 as the company entered a no-delivery period for the next one month.
Larsen and Toubro edged up 6.25 rupees higher 241.25.
However Hindustan Lever bucked the trend and lost 24.50 rupees to 1,294.00.
